questions.prompt: Select all true statements about BEAM processes compared to OS threads. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Each BEAM process has its own isolated heap and mailbox
A single BEAM node can run hundreds of thousands of concurrent processes
BEAM processes share a single mutable heap without message passing
BEAM processes are lightweight (~2 KB initial memory) and preemptively scheduled across CPU cores

questions.prompt: What happens when a process calls `send(pid, msg)`?

options.text: It blocks until `pid` finishes processing `msg`
It executes `msg` in the caller's process
It terminates `pid`
It copies `msg` asynchronously into `pid`'s mailbox and returns immediately

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between `Process.link/1` and `Process.monitor/1`?

options.text: Links are bidirectional crash propagation (unless `trap_exit` is true); monitors are unidirectional notifications delivering `{:DOWN, ref, :process, pid, reason}`
Links are unidirectional and monitors are bidirectional
Monitors kill the caller when the target exits
Links only work across different machines

questions.prompt: What does `Process.flag(:trap_exit, true)` do inside a process?

options.text: Ignores all incoming messages
Converts incoming exit signals from linked processes (except `:kill`) into `{:EXIT, from_pid, reason}` mailbox messages
Prevents the process from ever crashing
Disables `GenServer.call/3` timeouts

questions.prompt: In `receive do ... end`, what happens to messages in the mailbox that do NOT match any clause?

options.text: They are immediately deleted
They raise `MatchError`
They remain in the mailbox in order until a later `receive` matches them (or can cause unbounded mailbox growth if never matched)
They are sent back to the sender

questions.prompt: When should you use `Task.async/1` + `Task.await/2` vs `Task.Supervisor.start_child/2`?

options.text: Use `Task.async` for fire-and-forget work and `Task.Supervisor` when you need a return value
`Task.Supervisor` runs tasks synchronously in the caller
`Task.async` never times out
Use `Task.async/await` when the caller needs the result and should link to the task; use `Task.Supervisor` for isolated or fire-and-forget tasks

questions.prompt: What does `Task.async_stream(items, fun, max_concurrency: 8)` provide over spawning `Task.async` for every item in a huge list?

options.text: It bounds concurrency to `max_concurrency` workers and streams results with backpressure
It runs everything sequentially
It disables timeouts
It persists tasks to disk

questions.prompt: What is `Agent` best used for in Elixir?

options.text: CPU-intensive matrix multiplication
Simple state wrapper around a single process when you don't need custom `handle_info` or complex lifecycle callbacks
Replacing `Supervisor`
Distributed consensus

questions.prompt: Match each `GenServer` callback to what triggers it.

columns.label: Any other message sent to the process (e.g., `send/2`, `:DOWN`, timers)
Post-`init` or post-callback continuation before processing the mailbox

questions.prompt: Why is returning `{:ok, state, {:continue, :load_cache}}` from `GenServer.init/1` better than doing slow I/O directly in `init/1`?

options.text: `init/1` cannot call other modules
`{:continue, ...}` runs in a separate OS process
`init/1` blocks the parent `Supervisor` until it returns; `{:continue, ...}` unblocks the supervisor immediately while running setup before any mailbox messages
It skips `terminate/2`

questions.prompt: Why can a single `GenServer` become a scalability bottleneck if placed in front of every HTTP request?

options.text: `GenServer` cannot use `ETS`
`GenServer.call` always takes 5 seconds
`GenServer` only runs on one CPU core for the whole VM
A `GenServer` processes its mailbox sequentially one message at a time, serializing all callers

questions.prompt: What happens when `GenServer.call(pid, :work, 5_000)` times out on the caller?

options.text: The caller raises an exit (`:timeout`), while the `GenServer` may still finish processing `:work` unless handled
The `GenServer` is automatically killed
The message is removed from the `GenServer`'s mailbox
The BEAM node restarts

questions.prompt: Match each OTP `Supervisor` restart strategy to its behavior when a child crashes.

columns.label: Restarts only the crashed child process
Terminates and restarts all children in the supervisor
Terminates and restarts the crashed child plus any children started after it

questions.prompt: When should you use `DynamicSupervisor` instead of a static `Supervisor`?

options.text: When all children are known at boot time
When children are started and stopped dynamically on demand (e.g., one process per user session or job)
When you need `:one_for_all`
When you want to disable restarts

questions.prompt: Match each OTP child spec `restart:` option to its restart policy.

columns.label: Always restarts the child regardless of exit reason
Restarts only if the child exits abnormally (not `:normal`, `:shutdown`, `{:shutdown, _}`)

questions.prompt: What is `max_restarts` and `max_seconds` on a `Supervisor` for?

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `ETS` (Erlang Term Storage) in Elixir. (Select all that apply.)
